THE YOUNG MAKER PATH · AGES 10 TO 18

Not the same lesson for every age.

A ten-year-old should feel capable, not overwhelmed. An eighteen-year-old should feel challenged, not patronised. The projects, tools and independence grow with the learner.

Find the right starting point ↓

PLAY → BUILD → CREATE

THREE WAYS IN

Start at the level that feels exciting, not frightening.

Age is the guide. Experience decides the exact starting lesson.

10TO12

Code Explorers

Make the screen respond.

Stories, movement and games make invisible ideas easy to see.

They learn

  • Algorithms and clear instructions
  • Events, loops and conditions
  • Variables, coordinates and simple logic
  • Testing and finding small mistakes
  • Basic HTML and CSS
  • Safe and responsible internet habits
THEY BUILDAn animated story, a Scratch game and a one-page website.

TOOLS: SCRATCH · MAKECODE · HTML · CSS

Enter the ages 10 to 12 course →
13TO15

Code Builders

Move from blocks to typed code.

The learner keeps the visual confidence and begins controlling the details.

They learn

  • HTML structure and responsive CSS
  • JavaScript events and page interactions
  • Python variables, functions and lists
  • User input and basic validation
  • Data tables and simple visualisations
  • Debugging from error messages
THEY BUILDAn interactive website, a browser game and a useful Python program.

TOOLS: HTML · CSS · JAVASCRIPT · PYTHON

16TO18

Code Creators

Build work that can leave the classroom.

Projects begin with a person or problem, then move from sketch to a working release.

They learn

  • Structured JavaScript and Python
  • Git and version history
  • APIs and basic databases
  • Accessible, responsive interfaces
  • Input security and software testing
  • Responsible use of AI-generated code
THEY BUILDA deployed website, a data project and an original community-focused app.

TOOLS: JAVASCRIPT · PYTHON · GIT · APIS

THE COURSE JOURNEY

Eight missions. Each one unlocks a new kind of making.

01

Think like a computer

Sequences, instructions and breaking a problem into parts.

02

Bring a story to life

Events, movement, sound and choices that change what happens.

03

Build a game

Rules, scores, collisions, levels and testing with another learner.

04

Claim a place on the web

Structure, visual style, interaction and publishing.

05

Make decisions with code

Python or JavaScript programs that respond to real input.

06

Become a data detective

Collect, clean and question information before drawing conclusions.

07

Use AI without losing the thinking

Ask for hints, inspect generated code and test every claim.

08

Solve something real

Interview a user, build a first version, gather feedback and improve it.

THE REAL GRADUATION TEST

Give them a problem they have never seen before.

Can they understand it, break it down, try an approach, investigate the mistake, ask for useful help and explain the final result? That is the skill we are building.

What they leave with

  • 3 to 5 projectsWork they can open and demonstrate
  • Independent debugging habitsA method for getting unstuck
  • Clear explanationsThe ability to talk through their own code
  • A next directionWeb, Python, games, data, AI, robotics or security

THEIR FIRST PROJECT CAN START SMALL

Small is how capable begins.
